title: Linden Memberships Enrollment Terms, including Rejoining after Termination
content:
## Article 1: Choice of tier and dues cycle

A patient may enroll in a tier of Linden Memberships whose entry gate they meet, choosing a dues cycle that the tier offers. The primary member must be at least the tier's minimum age on the enrollment date.

## Article 2: Start of the membership

1. An enrollment opens the membership in status pending, with the chosen tier, the dues cycle, the dues per cycle (including any dependent add-ons) and the number of dependents covered.
2. The membership starts when the first dues and the tier's enrollment fee are paid. It then becomes active, and the records show its start date; its first period begins on that start date; its commitment end date is the start date plus the tier's minimum commitment months; and a monthly allotment of member visit credits is granted as of the start date.
3. An enrollment whose first dues remain unpaid once the tier's number of days to pay the first dues has run from the enrollment date is abandoned: the membership closes as cancelled, with enrollment abandoned as the reason.

## Article 3: Family coverage

A Linden Family Membership covers the tier's included number of dependents in the base dues and up to the tier's maximum number of dependents in total, each dependent beyond the included number adding the tier's dependent add-on per month. Dependents leave the membership at the tier's dependent age limit.

## Article 4: Rejoining after a termination for non-payment

1. A patient whose earlier membership was terminated for non-payment may not re-enroll during the waiting period.
2. The enrollment is made no earlier than the tier's rejoin waiting period counted from the date the earlier membership was terminated.
3. The waiting period is counted in calendar months from the termination date to the same day of the month, falling back to the last day of the month when that day does not exist, and enrollment on that day is allowed.
4. The evidence is the group's own record of the earlier membership: its status of terminated and the date it was closed. A patient's recollection of when a membership ended does not replace that record.
5. The terminations that matter are those of the patient's other memberships whose closing date falls within the tier's rejoin waiting period of calendar months ending on the enrollment date.

### Boundary cases (hypothetical dates and waiting periods)

| Earlier membership terminated | Waiting period | First day enrollment is allowed | Enrollment on the day before |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10 March | 12 months | 10 March of the following year | 9 March: not allowed |
| 15 January | 6 months | 15 July | 14 July: not allowed |
| 31 August | 6 months | 28 February (29 February in a leap year), because 31 February does not exist | 27 February: not allowed |
| 20 May | 0 months | 20 May, the termination date itself | none |

A cancellation at the member's own notice or an abandoned enrollment is not a termination for non-payment, and Article 4 does not apply to it.

## Article 5: Relation to insurance and the financial account

A membership is not insurance and never changes the tier of the patient's Patient Financial Account.
